title: Why Kearny stayed afloat
body:
Why didn't USS Kearny sink?

This morning's dispatch told how a U-boat torpedo tore into her off Iceland on 17 October 1941. Part of the answer to how she got home was built into her hull.

Kearny was a Gleaves class destroyer. Her designers split the machinery into two separate units, each with its own fireroom and engine room. The idea was simple: a single torpedo should not be able to cripple the whole ship.

That night it worked. Her crew held the flooding to the forward fire room, and power from the aft fire room carried her out of danger. She reached Iceland two days later.
threads:
Why didn't USS Kearny sink after a U-boat torpedo hit her on 17 October 1941?

Her Gleaves class design split the machinery into two separate units, each with its own fireroom and engine room, so one hit could not stop the whole ship.

Her crew held the flooding to the forward fire room, and power from the aft fire room carried her out of danger.
